subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the four-stroke diesel engine?

options.text: In C.I. engines, air-fuel mixture is sucked during the stroke and the fuel is injected in the cylinder near the end of the compression stroke.
The operation of C.I. engines (or diesel engines) is practically the same as those of S.I. engines.
In C.I. engines, only air is sucked during the stroke and the fuel is injected in the cylinder near the end of the compression stroke.
Cycles in both petrol and diesel engines consist of suction, compression, ignition, expansion and exhaust.

solution:
The correct answer is __Option 1__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Correct functioning of a four-stroke diesel engine__ includes distinct processes for air and fuel intake.
 
• In Compression Ignition (C.I.) engines, only air is sucked during the suction stroke.
 
• The fuel is injected into the cylinder near the end of the compression stroke where it mixes with compressed air.
 
• Statement in Option 1 is incorrect, as it falsely mentions that an air-fuel mixture is sucked during the stroke, which applies to Spark Ignition (S.I.) engines, not diesel engines.
 
• Both diesel and petrol engines consist of four cycles: suction, compression, ignition, expansion, and exhaust, but their operation differs in fuel intake and ignition processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Spark Ignition (S.I.) Engines:**
 
 
• In S.I. engines, an air-fuel mixture is introduced into the cylinder during the suction stroke.
 
• Ignition occurs via a spark plug.
 
 
 
• **Compression Ignition (C.I.) Engines:**
 
 
• In C.I. engines, only air is sucked during the suction stroke.
 
• Fuel is injected into the compressed air at high pressure and ignites due to the heat of compression.
